competition: Czech-Slovak Mathematical Olympiad (National Final, Category A)

problems.problem: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that the sum $4\cdot 3^{2^n}+3\cdot 4^{2^n}$ is divisible by $13$ if and only if $n$ is even.

An isosceles triangle $ABC$ with base $AB$ is given. A point $P$ is chosen on its altitude $CD$ so that the incircles of the triangle $ABP$ and of the quadrilateral $PECF$ are congruent; here $E$ is the intersection of the line $AP$ with the side $BC$ and $F$ is the intersection of the line $BP$ with the side $AC$. Prove that the incircles of the triangles $ADP$ and $BCP$ are also congruent.

In the plane, $2000$ congruent triangles of area $1$ are given, which are images of one and the same triangle under different translations. Each of these triangles contains the centroids of all the others. Prove that the area of the union of these triangles is less than $\frac{22}{9}$.

For which quadratic functions $f(x)$ does there exist a quadratic function $g(x)$ such that the roots of the equation $g\bigl(f(x)\bigr)=0$ are four distinct consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression and at the same time they are also roots of the equation $f(x)g(x)=0$?

Monika made a paper model of a triangular pyramid whose base was a right triangle. When she cut the model along the legs of the base and along a median of one of the faces, after unfolding it into the plane she obtained a square with side $a$. Determine the volume of this pyramid.
Find all four-digit numbers $\overline{abcd}$ (in the decimal system) for which the equality $$\overline{abcd}+1=(\overline{ac}+1)(\overline{bd}+1)$$ holds.
Determine all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that for all real numbers $x$ $$\bigl(P(x)\bigr)^2+P(-x)=P(x^2)+P(x).$$

In the plane, a triangle $PQX$ is given with $|PQ|=3\text{ cm}$, $|PX|=2.6\text{ cm}$, $|QX|=3.8\text{ cm}$. Construct a right triangle $ABC$ such that its incircle touches the hypotenuse $AB$ at the point $P$ and the leg $BC$ at the point $Q$, and such that the point $X$ lies on the line $AC$.
Find all triples of real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ for which the set of all solutions of the inequality $$\sqrt{2x^2+ax+b}>x-c$$ with unknown $x$ is the set $(-\infty,0]\cup(1,\infty)$.

A certain language has $n$ letters. A group of letters (written one after another) is a word if and only if there are no two equal letters between any two equal letters. Determine the number of all words of maximal length.

An isosceles trapezoid $C_1AB_2C_2$ with the shorter base $B_2C_2$ was cut out of paper. Let $B_1$ be the foot of the perpendicular from the midpoint $D$ of the leg $C_1C_2$ to the base $AC_1$. After folding the paper along the segments $DB_1$, $AD$ and $AC_2$, the points $C_1$, $C_2$ moved in space into one point $C$ and the points $B_1$, $B_2$ into the point $B$. This produced a model of a tetrahedron $ABCD$ with volume $64\text{ cm}^3$. Determine the side lengths of the original trapezoid.

Positive integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ are given, together with a function $f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=1$ for every integer $x<0$ and $$f(x)=1-f(x-a_1)\,f(x-a_2)\cdots f(x-a_n)$$ for every integer $x\ge 0$. Prove that there exist positive integers $s$ and $t$ such that $f(x+t)=f(x)$ for every integer $x>s$.
Solve in the set of integers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}(4x)_5+7y&=14,\\(2y)_5-(3x)_7&=74,\end{aligned}$$ where $(n)_k$ denotes the multiple of the number $k$ closest to the number $n$.

Consider an arbitrary equilateral triangle $KLM$ whose vertices $K$, $L$ and $M$ lie on the sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CD$, respectively, of a given square $ABCD$. Find the set of midpoints of the sides of all such triangles $KLM$.

Prove that a positive integer $A$ is the square of a positive integer if and only if for every positive integer $n$ at least one of the differences $$(A+1)^2-A,\ (A+2)^2-A,\ (A+3)^2-A,\ \dots,\ (A+n)^2-A$$ is divisible by $n$.
Find all pairs of real numbers $a$, $b$ for which the equation $$\frac{ax^2-24x+b}{x^2-1}=x$$ has exactly two solutions in the set of real numbers, and the sum of these solutions is $12$.

In the plane, a triangle $KLM$ is given, together with a point $A$ lying on the ray opposite to the ray $KL$. Construct a rectangle $ABCD$ whose vertices $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on the lines $KM$, $KL$ and $LM$, respectively.

Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ satisfying, for arbitrary $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^+$, the equality $$f\bigl(xf(y)\bigr)=f(xy)+x.$$
Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}x^2-xy+y^2&=7,\\x^2y+xy^2&=-2.\end{aligned}$$

Points $D$, $E$, $F$ are chosen in the interiors of the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, of a given triangle $ABC$ so that the segments $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ intersect at one point, which we denote by $G$. Prove that if circles can be inscribed in the quadrilaterals $AFGE$, $BDGF$, $CEGD$ such that each two of them are externally tangent, then the triangle $ABC$ is equilateral.

A sequence $(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ with the first term $x_1=1$ satisfies, for every $n>1$, the condition $$x_n=\pm(n-1)x_{n-1}\pm(n-2)x_{n-2}\pm\dots\pm 2x_2\pm x_1$$ for a suitable choice of the signs “$+$” and “$-$”. Decide whether it is possible that the inequality $x_n\ne 12$ holds for only finitely many indices $n$.

An obtuse angle $AKS$ is given in the plane. Construct a triangle $ABC$ such that its side $BC$ lies on the line $KS$, the point $S$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and the point $K$ is the intersection of $BC$ with the bisector of the opposite angle $BAC$.

Show that in the numeral system with an arbitrary base $z\ge 3$ there exist two-digit numbers $A$ and $B$ which differ only in the order of their digits and have the following property: the quadratic equation $x^2-Ax+B=0$ has a double root in the set of real numbers. Prove also that for a given base $z$ such a pair $A$, $B$ is unique. For example, in the decimal system ($z=10$) these are only the numbers $A=18$ and $B=81$.
Prove that if the product of positive numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ equals $1$, then $$\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{a}\ge a+b+c.$$
Determine all triples $(x,y,z)$ of real numbers for which $$x^2+y^2+z^2\le 6+\min\left\{x^2-\frac{8}{x^4},\ y^2-\frac{8}{y^4},\ z^2-\frac{8}{z^4}\right\}.$$

For an arbitrary positive integer $n$, form from the letters $A$ and $B$ all possible “words” of length $n$, and let $p_n$ denote the number of those which contain neither four consecutive letters $AAAA$ nor three consecutive letters $BBB$. Determine the value of the expression $$\frac{p_{2004}-p_{2002}-p_{1999}}{p_{2001}+p_{2000}}.$$

In the plane, a circle $k$ and $121$ of its secants $p_1,p_2,\dots,p_{121}$ are given. On each line $p_i$ a point $A_i$ lying inside the circle is given. Prove that there exists a point $X$ on the circle $k$ such that the segment $A_iX$ forms an angle less than $21^\circ$ with the line $p_i$ for at least $29$ different indices $i$.
Determine for which positive integers $n$ the sum $$\frac{n}{1!}+\frac{n}{2!}+\dots+\frac{n}{n!}$$ is an integer.

Let $L$ be an arbitrary interior point of the shorter arc $CD$ of the circumcircle of a square $ABCD$. Let $K$ be the intersection of the lines $AL$ and $CD$, $M$ the intersection of the lines $AD$ and $CL$, and $N$ the intersection of the lines $MK$ and $BC$. Prove that the points $B$, $L$, $M$, $N$ lie on one circle.

Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ be the set of all positive real numbers. Determine all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ which satisfy, for all positive numbers $x$, $y$, the equality $$x^2\bigl(f(x)+f(y)\bigr)=(x+y)\,f\bigl(f(x)y\bigr).$$

Consider arbitrary arithmetic progressions of real numbers $(x_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ and $(y_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ which have the same first term and satisfy, for some $k>1$, the equalities $$x_{k-1}y_{k-1}=42,\qquad x_ky_k=30\qquad\text{and}\qquad x_{k+1}y_{k+1}=16.$$ Find all such progressions for which the index $k$ is the largest possible.

Determine for which $m$ there exist exactly $2^{15}$ subsets $X$ of the set $\{1,2,3,\dots,47\}$ with the following property: the number $m$ is the smallest element of the set $X$, and for every $x\in X$ either $x+m\in X$ or $x+m>47$.

In a trapezoid $ABCD$ ($AB\parallel CD$), let $E$ be the midpoint of the leg $BC$. Prove that if both quadrilaterals $ABED$ and $AECD$ are tangential, then the side lengths of the trapezoid $ABCD$, denoted in the usual way, satisfy the equalities $$a+c=\frac{b}{3}+d\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{3}{b}.$$

An acute triangle $AKL$ is given in the plane. Consider an arbitrary rectangle $ABCD$ circumscribed about the triangle $AKL$ so that the point $K$ lies on the side $BC$ and the point $L$ lies on the side $CD$. Determine the locus of the intersections $S$ of the diagonals $AC$, $BD$ of all such rectangles $ABCD$.

Prove that for arbitrary real numbers $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ with $q\ne -1$ and $s\ne -1$ the following holds: the quadratic equations $$x^2+px+q=0,\qquad x^2+rx+s=0$$ have a common root in the set of real numbers and their other roots are reciprocals of each other if and only if the coefficients $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ satisfy the equalities $$pr=(q+1)(s+1)\qquad\text{and}\qquad p(q+1)s=r(s+1)q.$$ (A double root of a quadratic equation is counted twice.)

Decide whether for every ordering of the numbers $1,2,3,\dots,15$ these numbers can be written in at most four different colours so that all numbers of the same colour form, in the given order, a monotonic (i.e. increasing or decreasing) sequence. (A one-term sequence is monotonic.)

A sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers has the property that for every $n\ge 1$ we have $a_{n+1}=a_n+b_n$, where $b_n$ is the number whose digits are those of $a_n$ in reverse order (unlike the notation of $a_n$, the notation of $b_n$ may begin with one or more zeros). For example, for $a_1=170$ we get $a_2=241$, $a_3=383$, $a_4=766$, $\dots$ Decide whether $a_7$ can be a prime.
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers such that the equation $$(x+m)(x+n)=x+m+n$$ has at least one integer solution. Prove that $$\frac{1}{2}<\frac{m}{n}<2.$$

In a triangle $ABC$ which is not equilateral, let $K$ be the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $BAC$ with the side $BC$, and $L$ the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $ABC$ with the side $AC$. Further, let $S$ be the incentre, $O$ the circumcentre and $V$ the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$. Prove that the following two statements are equivalent:

a) The line $KL$ is tangent to the circumcircles of the triangles $ALS$, $BVS$ and $BKS$.

b) The points $A$, $B$, $K$, $L$ and $O$ lie on one circle.

A segment $AB$ is given in the plane. Determine the locus of the centroids of all acute triangles $ABC$ with the following property: the vertices $A$ and $B$, the orthocentre $V$ and the incentre $S$ of the triangle $ABC$ lie on one circle.
Find all triples of pairwise distinct primes $p$, $q$, $r$ satisfying the following conditions: $$\begin{aligned}p&\mid q+r,\\q&\mid r+2p,\\r&\mid p+3q.\end{aligned}$$
Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}\tan^2 x+2\cot^2 2y&=1,\\\tan^2 y+2\cot^2 2z&=1,\\\tan^2 z+2\cot^2 2x&=1.\end{aligned}$$

A piece is placed on some square of an $n\times n$ chessboard ($n\ge 2$) and is then moved alternately “diagonally” and “straight”. “Diagonally” means to a square that has exactly one point in common with the previous one. “Straight” means to an adjacent square that has a common side with the previous one. Determine all $n$ for which there exist a starting square and a sequence of moves beginning with a “diagonal” move such that the piece passes through the whole chessboard and visits every square exactly once.

In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $L$, $M$ be the incentres of the triangles $BCA$, $BCD$, respectively. Further, let $R$ be the intersection of the perpendiculars drawn from the points $L$ and $M$ to the lines $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Prove that the triangle $LMR$ is isosceles.

Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the set of all positive integers and consider all functions $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for arbitrary $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$ $$f\bigl(xf(y)\bigr)=yf(x).$$ Determine the smallest possible value of $f(2007)$.

A set $M$ contains all positive integers from $1$ to $2007$ inclusive and has the following property: if a number $n$ is an element of the set $M$, then all terms of the arithmetic progression with first term $n$ and common difference $n+1$ lie in $M$. Decide whether the set $M$ must contain all positive integers greater than some number $m$.

An acute triangle $ABC$ with $|AC|\ne|BC|$ is given. Consider points $D$ and $E$ in the interiors of its sides $BC$ and $AC$, respectively, for which $ABDE$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Let $P$ be the intersection of its diagonals $AD$ and $BE$. Prove that if the lines $CP$ and $AB$ are perpendicular, then $P$ is the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$.
Determine all ordered triples $(x,y,z)$ of pairwise distinct real numbers which satisfy the set equation $$\{x,y,z\}=\left\{\frac{x-y}{y-z},\ \frac{y-z}{z-x},\ \frac{z-x}{x-y}\right\}.$$
Determine the coefficients $p$, $q$, $r$ of the polynomial $f(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ if you know that they are nonzero pairwise distinct integers and that $f(p)=p^3$, $f(q)=q^3$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $|AC|\ne|BC|$, let $D$ and $E$ be the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$. Let $V$ be the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$, $F$ the intersection of the lines $AB$ and $DE$, and $S$ the midpoint of the side $AB$. Further, let $K$ be the intersection of the circumcircles of the triangles $BDS$ and $AES$ different from the point $S$.

a) Prove that the points $D$, $E$, $V$, $K$ lie on one circle.

b) Prove that the points $F$, $V$, $K$ lie on one line.

In an $n\times n$ table, where $n\ge 2$, all the numbers $1,2,\dots,n^2$ are written row by row in this order (the first row contains the numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ in succession, the second row $n+1,n+2,\dots,2n$, etc.). In one step we may choose any two numbers in adjacent cells (i.e. cells having a common side) and either increase both of them by $1$ or decrease both of them by $1$. For which $n$ is it possible to obtain, after a finite number of steps, a table in which all numbers are equal to $365$?
Prove that for no positive integer $n$ is the number $27^n-n^{27}$ a prime.
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers whose product is $1$. Prove that if $k$, $m$ are positive integers with $k>m$, then $$x^k+y^k+z^k\ge x^m+y^m+z^m.$$
Prove that if all of the numbers $p$, $3p+2$, $5p+4$, $7p+6$, $9p+8$ and $11p+10$ are primes, then the number $6p+11$ is composite.

On the shorter of the arcs $CD$ of the circumcircle of a rectangle $ABCD$, choose a point $P$. Denote by $K$, $L$ and $M$ the feet of the perpendiculars from $P$ to the lines $AB$, $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Show that the angle $LKM$ measures $45^\circ$ if and only if $ABCD$ is a square.

Find the smallest positive number $x$ with the following property: if $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ are arbitrary positive numbers whose product is $1$, then $$a^x+b^x+c^x+d^x\ge \frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}+\frac{1}{d}.$$

We investigate for which positive integers $n$ there exist exactly four positive integers $k$ such that the number $n+k$ is a divisor of the number $n+k^2$.

a) Show that $n=58$ has this property and find the corresponding four numbers $k$.

b) Prove that an even number $n=2p$, where $p\ge 3$, has this property if and only if both $p$ and $2p+1$ are primes.

(Zero is not counted among the natural numbers.)

At each vertex of a regular $n$-gon $A_1A_2\dots A_n$ there lies a certain number of coins: at the vertex $A_k$ there are exactly $k$ coins, $1\le k\le n$. We choose two coins and move each of them to a neighbouring vertex in such a way that one of them moves clockwise and the other one counterclockwise. Decide for which $n$ it is possible, after a finite number of such moves, to achieve that for every $k$, $1\le k\le n$, there are $n+1-k$ coins at the vertex $A_k$.

Two distinct points $O$ and $T$ are given in a plane $\omega$. Find the set of vertices of all triangles which lie in the plane $\omega$ and have centroid at the point $T$ and circumcentre at the point $O$.
Determine all pairs of positive integers $a$, $b$ such that $$4^a+4a^2+4=b^2.$$
A circular target of radius $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ has been hit by $19$ shots. Prove that the distance between some two of the hits is less than $7\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Rumburak kidnapped to his castle $31$ members of party $A$, $28$ members of party $B$, $23$ members of party $C$ and $19$ members of party $D$, and locked each of them in a separate cell. After work they could occasionally walk in the courtyard and talk. As soon as three members of three different parties started talking together, Rumburak, as a punishment, re-registered them into the fourth party. (Never did more than three of the kidnapped talk together.)

a) Could it happen that after some time all the kidnapped were members of one party? Of which one?

b) Determine all quadruples of positive integers whose sum is $101$ and which, as the numbers of kidnapped members of the four parties, make it possible that, thanks to Rumburak, all of them eventually become members of one party.

A circle $k$ with a chord $AC$ which is not a diameter is given. On its tangent through the point $A$ we choose a point $X\ne A$ and denote by $D$ the intersection of the circle $k$ with the interior of the segment $XC$ (if it exists). We complete the triangle $ACD$ to a trapezoid $ABCD$ inscribed in the circle $k$. Determine the locus of the intersections of the lines $BC$ and $AD$ corresponding to all such trapezoids.

The numbers $1, 2, \dots, 33$ are written on a blackboard. In one step we choose two numbers written on the blackboard whose product is a perfect square, erase both chosen numbers and write the square root of their product on the blackboard. We continue in this way until only numbers remain on the blackboard such that the product of no two of them is a perfect square. (In one step we may also erase two equal numbers and replace them by the same number.) Prove that at least $16$ numbers remain on the blackboard.

Find the minimum of the expression $$\frac{a+b+c}{2}-\frac{[a,b]+[b,c]+[c,a]}{a+b+c},$$ where the variables $a$, $b$, $c$ are arbitrary integers greater than $1$ and $[x,y]$ denotes the least common multiple of the numbers $x$, $y$.

Determine the sizes of the interior angles of all triangles $ABC$ with the following property: there exist points $K$, $M$ in the interiors of the sides $AB$, $AC$, respectively, which together with the intersection $L$ of the lines $MB$ and $KC$ form cyclic quadrilaterals $AKLM$ and $KBCM$ with congruent circumcircles.
Determine all triples of primes $(p,q,r)$ such that $$(p+1)(q+2)(r+3)=4pqr.$$

Suppose that real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ satisfy the system of equations $$x+y+z=12,\qquad x^2+y^2+z^2=54.$$ Prove that then the following statements hold:

a) Each of the numbers $xy$, $yz$, $zx$ is at least $9$ but at most $25$.

b) One of the numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ is at most $3$ and another one of them is at least $5$.

Consider a quadratic trinomial $ax^2+bx+c$ with real coefficients $a\ge 2$, $b\ge 2$, $c\ge 2$. Adam and Boris play the following game: when it is Adam's turn, he chooses one of the coefficients of the trinomial and replaces it by the *sum* of the other two. When it is Boris's turn, he chooses one of the coefficients and replaces it by the *product* of the other two. Adam starts and the players alternate regularly. The winner is the player after whose move the resulting trinomial has two distinct real roots. Depending on the coefficients $a$, $b$, $c$ of the initial trinomial, determine which of the players has a winning strategy.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ which is not equilateral, denote by $P$ the foot of the altitude from the vertex $C$ to the side $AB$, by $V$ the orthocenter, by $O$ the circumcentre, by $D$ the intersection of the ray $CO$ with the side $AB$ and by $E$ the midpoint of the segment $CD$. Prove that the line $EP$ passes through the midpoint of the segment $OV$.

Denote by $\mathbb{R}^+$ the set of all positive real numbers. Determine all functions $f\colon \mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ such that for all $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^+$ $$f(x)\cdot f(y)=f(y)\cdot f\bigl(x\cdot f(y)\bigr)+\frac{1}{xy}.$$
Find all integers $n$ for which $n^4-3n^2+9$ is a prime.
Find the largest possible area of a triangle $ABC$ whose medians have lengths satisfying the inequalities $t_a\le 2$, $t_b\le 3$, $t_c\le 4$.
Prove that among any $101$ real numbers there exist two numbers $u$ and $v$ such that $$100\,|u-v|\cdot|1-uv|\le (1+u^2)(1+v^2).$$

A point $X$ is given in the interior of a parallelogram $ABCD$. Construct a line which passes through the point $X$ and divides the given parallelogram into two parts whose areas differ from each other as much as possible.

In a group of $90$ children, each child has at least $30$ friends (friendship is mutual). Prove that the children can be divided into three groups of $30$ in such a way that each child has at least one friend in its own group.
Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} x^4+y^2+4&=5yz,\\ y^4+z^2+4&=5zx,\\ z^4+x^2+4&=5xy. \end{aligned}$$
Find all pairs of integers $a$, $b$ for which the equality $$\frac{a^2+1}{2b^2-3}=\frac{a-1}{2b-1}$$ holds.

Each of the robbers in a band of $n$ members ($n\ge 3$) has plundered a certain number of coins. Altogether $100n$ coins were plundered. The robbers decided to share the loot in the following way: in each step, one of the robbers gives one coin to each of two other robbers. Find all positive integers $n\ge 3$ for which, after a finite number of steps, each robber can have $100$ coins, regardless of how many coins the individual robbers plundered.

In a parallelogram $ABCD$ with centre $S$, denote by $O$ the centre of the incircle of the triangle $ABD$ and by $T$ its point of tangency with the diagonal $BD$. Prove that the lines $OS$ and $CT$ are parallel.

A positive integer $N$ is written on a blackboard in the decimal system. If it is not a one-digit number, we erase its last digit $c$ and replace the number $m$ which remains on the blackboard by the number $|m-3c|$. (For example, if the number $N=1204$ was on the blackboard, after the operation there will be $120-3\cdot 4=108$.) Find all positive integers $N$ from which, by repeating the described operation, we eventually obtain the number $0$.

A parallelogram $ABCD$ is given such that the feet $K$, $L$ of the perpendiculars dropped from the point $D$ to the sides $AB$, $BC$, respectively, are interior points of these sides. Prove that $KL\parallel AC$ if and only if $$|\angle BCA|+|\angle ABD|=|\angle BDA|+|\angle ACD|.$$
Find all positive real numbers $p$ such that $$\sqrt{a^2+pb^2}+\sqrt{b^2+pa^2}\ge a+b+(p-1)\sqrt{ab}$$ holds for every pair of positive real numbers $a$, $b$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Denote all its positive divisors by $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_k$ so that $d_1<d_2<\dots<d_k$ (i.e. $d_1=1$ and $d_k=n$). Determine all values of $n$ for which $d_5-d_3=50$ and $11d_5+8d_7=3n$.

In a plane in which a segment $AB$ is given, consider triangles $XYZ$ such that $X$ is an interior point of the segment $AB$, the triangles $XBY$ and $XZA$ are similar ($\triangle XBY\sim\triangle XZA$), and the points $A$, $B$, $Y$, $Z$ lie on a circle in this order. Find the locus of the midpoints of all the segments $YZ$.

Consider an $8\times 8$ chessboard, and next to each \"edge\" separating two of its squares write the positive integer equal to the number of ways in which the whole chessboard can be cut into $2\times 1$ rectangles so that the edge in question is part of the cut. Determine the last digit of the sum of all numbers written in this way.

$234$ spectators came to a cinema. Determine for which $n\ge 4$ it could happen that the spectators could be seated in $n$ rows so that each spectator in the $i$-th row knew exactly $j$ spectators in the $j$-th row, for any $i, j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, $i\ne j$. (The relation of acquaintance is mutual.)

An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. Denote by $k$ the circle with diameter $AB$. The circle which touches the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ at the point $A$ and passes through the point $C$ intersects the circle $k$ at a point $P$, $P\ne A$. The circle which touches the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ at the point $B$ and passes through the point $C$ intersects the circle $k$ at a point $Q$, $Q\ne B$. Prove that the intersection of the lines $AQ$ and $BP$ lies on the angle bisector of $\angle ACB$.
Prove that for any non-negative real numbers $a$ and $b$ the inequality $$\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2+1}}+\frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+1}}\ge\frac{a+b}{\sqrt{ab+1}}$$ holds, and determine when equality occurs.

For a given positive integer $n$, determine the number of paths of length $2n+2$ from the point $[0,0]$ to the point $[n,n]$ which do not pass through any point more than once. By a path of length $2n+2$ from the point $[0,0]$ to the point $[n,n]$ we mean a $(2n+2)$-term sequence $$(A_0A_1, A_1A_2, A_2A_3, \dots, A_{2n+1}A_{2n+2})$$ of segments joining two neighbouring lattice points, where $A_0=[0,0]$, $A_{2n+2}=[n,n]$.

In an arbitrary triangle $ABC$ in which the median from the vertex $C$ is perpendicular neither to the side $CA$ nor to the side $CB$, denote by $X$ and $Y$ the intersections of the perpendicular bisector of this median with the lines $CA$ and $CB$. Find all such triangles $ABC$ for which the points $A$, $B$, $X$, $Y$ lie on a circle.
Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} a(b^2+c)&=c(c+ab),\\ b(c^2+a)&=a(a+bc),\\ c(a^2+b)&=b(b+ca). \end{aligned}$$

A triangle $ABC$ is given in which any two sides differ in length by at least $d>0$. Denote by $T$ its centroid, by $I$ the centre of its incircle and by $\varrho$ the radius of the incircle. Prove that $$S_{AIT}+S_{BIT}+S_{CIT}\ge\frac{2}{3}d\varrho,$$ where $S_{XYZ}$ denotes the area of the triangle $XYZ$.

A positive integer $n>2$ is given. Determine the largest integer $d$ for which the following statement holds: from any $n$-element set of integers one can choose three distinct non-empty subsets such that the sum of the elements of each of them is an integer multiple of the number $d$. (The chosen subsets may have common elements.)

Let $p>3$ be a given prime. Determine the number of all ordered six-tuples $(a,b,c,d,e,f)$ of positive integers whose sum equals $3p$ and such that all the fractions $$\frac{a+b}{c+d},\quad \frac{b+c}{d+e},\quad \frac{c+d}{e+f},\quad \frac{d+e}{f+a},\quad \frac{e+f}{a+b}$$ have integer values.

Denote by $r$ and $r_a$ the radii of the incircle and of the excircle opposite to the side $BC$ of a triangle $ABC$, respectively. Prove that if $$r+r_a=|BC|,$$ then the triangle $ABC$ is right-angled.

Mathematical clubs are popular among the inhabitants of a certain town. Any two of the clubs have at least one common member. Prove that we can distribute compasses and rulers to the inhabitants of the town in such a way that only one inhabitant gets both, and yet each club, at full attendance of its members, has at its disposal both a ruler and a compass.
Positive numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy $$(a+c)(b^2+ac)=4a.$$ Determine the maximum value of the expression $b+c$ and find all triples of numbers $(a,b,c)$ for which the expression attains this value.

In a triangle $ABC$ we have $|BC|=1$ and, moreover, there exists exactly one point $D$ on the side $BC$ such that $|DA|^2=|DB|\cdot|DC|$. Determine all possible values of the perimeter of the triangle $ABC$.

A piece called a prince is placed on some square of a $6\times 6$ chessboard. In one move it can jump either vertically or horizontally. The length of the jump is alternately one and two squares, the piece starting with a jump of length one (i.e. to a neighbouring square). Decide whether the starting position of the piece can be chosen so that, after a suitable sequence of $35$ jumps, it visits every square of the chessboard exactly once.

There are $100$ diamonds in a pile, of which $50$ are genuine and $50$ are fake. We invited a peculiar expert, the only one who can tell which are which. Every time we show him some three diamonds, he chooses two of them and (truthfully) tells us how many of these two are genuine. Decide whether we can surely identify all the genuine diamonds, regardless of how the expert chooses the pairs to be assessed.
Find all pairs of real numbers $k$, $l$ such that the inequality $$ka^2+lb^2>c^2$$ holds for the side lengths $a$, $b$, $c$ of any triangle.
Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$, $y$ $$f(y-xy)=f(x)y+(x-1)^2f(y).$$

To each sequence consisting of $n$ zeros and $n$ ones we assign the number of blocks of equal digits in it. (For example, the sequence $00111001$ has $4$ such blocks: $00$, $111$, $00$, $1$.) For a given $n$ we add up all the numbers assigned to all such sequences. Prove that the resulting sum equals $$(n+1)\binom{2n}{n}.$$

An acute triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$ is given. The angle bisector of $\angle BHC$ intersects the side $BC$ at a point $D$. Denote by $E$ and $F$ the images of the point $D$ under the reflections in the lines $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle $AEF$ passes through the midpoint of the arc $BAC$.
A non-zero integer $k$ is given. Prove that the equation $$k=\frac{x^2-xy+2y^2}{x+y}$$ is satisfied by an odd number of ordered pairs of integers $(x,y)$ if and only if $k$ is divisible by seven.

In a group of people, some pairs are friends. For a positive integer $k\ge 3$ we say that the group is $k$-good if every $k$-tuple of people from the group can be seated around a round table so that every two neighbours are friends. Prove that if the group is $6$-good, then it is also $7$-good.

Real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ are chosen so that the numbers $$\frac{1}{|x^2+2yz|},\quad \frac{1}{|y^2+2zx|},\quad \frac{1}{|z^2+2xy|}$$ are the side lengths of a (non-degenerate) triangle. Determine all possible values of the expression $xy+yz+zx$.

A triangle $ABC$ is given. The angle bisector at vertex $A$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $E$, $F$ be the circumcentres of triangles $ABD$, $ACD$, respectively. What can the measure of angle $BAC$ be if the circumcentre of triangle $AEF$ lies on the line $BC$?

Consider an arbitrary triple of integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ which are the side lengths of a triangle, have no common divisor greater than $1$, and for which the values of all three fractions $$\frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{a+b-c},\quad \frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{b+c-a},\quad \frac{c^2+a^2-b^2}{c+a-b}$$ are integers. Prove that the product of the denominators of these three fractions or its double is the square of an integer.

An isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with the longer base $AB$ is given. Let $I$ be the incentre of triangle $ABC$ and $J$ the centre of the excircle of triangle $ACD$ opposite to side $AD$. Prove that the lines $IJ$ and $AB$ are parallel.

Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for any colouring of the numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, n$ with three colours there exist two numbers of the same colour among them whose difference is the square of a positive integer.
Solve the system of equations in the set of real numbers: $$\begin{aligned} x^2-yz&=|y-z|+1,\\ y^2-zx&=|z-x|+1,\\ z^2-xy&=|x-y|+1.\end{aligned}$$

A rectangle $ABCD$ with $|AB|=a\ge b=|BC|$ is given. Construct points $P$ and $Q$ on the line $BD$ such that $|AP|=|PQ|=|QC|$. Discuss the solvability of the problem with respect to the lengths $a$, $b$.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $n$ be positive integers such that the following conditions hold:
(i) the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $a+b+c$ are pairwise coprime;
(ii) the number $(a+b+c)(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)(ab+bc+ca)$ is the $n$-th power of an integer.
Prove that the product $abc$ can be written as the difference of two $n$-th powers of integers.

An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. On the ray opposite to the ray $BC$ lies a point $P$ such that $|AB|=|BP|$. Analogously, on the ray opposite to the ray $CB$ lies a point $Q$ such that $|AC|=|CQ|$. Let $J$ be the centre of the excircle of the triangle opposite to side $BC$, and let $D$, $E$ be its points of tangency with the lines $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Suppose that the rays opposite to the rays $DP$ and $EQ$ intersect at a point $F$ different from $J$. Prove that $AF\perp FJ$.
Prove that there exist infinitely many integers which cannot be expressed in the form $2^a+3^b-5^c$, where $a$, $b$, $c$ are non-negative integers.

For which positive integers $n$ is it possible to write all the integers from $1$ to $n^2$ into an $n\times n$ table so that the arithmetic mean of the numbers in every row and in every column of the table is an integer?

Two positive integers $m$ and $n$ are written on a board. In each step, we replace one of the two numbers on the board by either their sum, or their product, or their quotient (if it is an integer). Depending on the numbers $m$ and $n$, determine all pairs that can appear on the board after several steps.

A triangle $ABC$ is given. Points $X$ and $Y$ are chosen in the interiors of its sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $Z$ be the intersection of the segments $BY$ and $CX$. Prove the inequality $$[BZX]+[CZY]>2[XYZ],$$ where $[DEF]$ denotes the area of triangle $DEF$.

Consider the system of equations $$\begin{aligned} x^2-3y+p&=z,\\ y^2-3z+p&=x,\\ z^2-3x+p&=y\end{aligned}$$ with a real parameter $p$.
a) For $p\ge 4$, solve the system in the set of real numbers.
b) Prove that for $p\in[1,4)$ every real solution of the system satisfies $x=y=z$.
Positive integers $a$, $b$ satisfy the equality $b^2=a^2+ab+b$. Prove that $b$ is the square of a positive integer.

An isosceles triangle $ABC$ with base $BC$ is given, and a point $D$ is chosen in the interior of the base. Let $E$, $F$ be points on the sides $AB$, $AC$, respectively, such that $\angle BED=\angle DFC>90^\circ$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $ABF$ and $AEC$ intersect on the line $AD$ at a point different from $A$.

For every positive integer $k$, let $P(k)$ denote the number of all positive $4k$-digit integers which can be formed from the digits $2$, $0$ and which are divisible by $2\,020$. Prove the inequality $$P(k)\ge \binom{2k-1}{k}^2$$ and determine all $k$ for which equality holds.
(Note. The decimal representation of a positive integer cannot begin with the digit $0$.)

A fraction with $1010$ boxes in the numerator and $1011$ boxes in the denominator serves as the game board for a two-player game: $$\frac{\square+\square+\dots+\square}{\square+\square+\dots+\square+\square}$$ The players alternate in turns. In each turn, a player chooses one of the numbers $1, 2, \dots, 2021$ and places it into any empty box. Each number may be used only once. The starting player wins if, after all the boxes are filled, the value of the fraction differs from the number $1$ by less than $10^{-6}$. Otherwise the second player wins. Decide which of the players has a winning strategy.

Let $I$ be the incentre of a right triangle $ABC$ with the right angle at vertex $A$. Further, let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the segments $AB$ and $BI$. Prove that the line $CI$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BMN$.

Pairwise distinct non-zero real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy the set equality $$\{a+b,\,b+c,\,c+a\}=\{ab,\,bc,\,ca\}.$$ Prove that the equality $$\{a,\,b,\,c\}=\{a^2-2,\,b^2-2,\,c^2-2\}$$ also holds.

Find all positive integers $n$ for which the equality $$n+d(n)+d(d(n))+\dots=2021$$ holds, where $d(0)=d(1)=0$ and for $k>1$, $d(k)$ is the superdivisor of the number $k$ (i.e. its largest divisor $d$ with the property $d<k$).

We call a string of characters neat if it has even length and its first half is identical to its second half (e.g. $abab$). We call a string nice if it can be split into several neat strings (such as $abcabcdedeff$ into $abcabc$, $dede$ and $ff$). A reduction of a string is an operation in which we erase two equal adjacent characters from the string (e.g. the string $abbac$ can be reduced to $aac$ and that further to $c$). Prove that any string containing each of its characters an even number of times can be obtained by a series of reductions from a suitable nice string.

An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. For each of its interior points $X$, let $X_a$, $X_b$, $X_c$ be its images under the reflections in the lines $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively. Prove that all the triangles $X_aX_bX_c$ have a common point.

$71$ non-zero real numbers are written in a row next to each other on a sheet of paper. Every number except the first and the last is $1$ less than the product of its two neighbours. Prove that the first and the last numbers are equal.

We say that a positive integer $d$ is fair if the number of $2021$-digit palindromes which are multiples of $d$ is the same as the number of $2022$-digit palindromes which are multiples of $d$. Does the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 35\}$ contain more numbers that are fair, or more that are not fair?
(A palindrome is a positive integer whose decimal representation reads the same from left to right as from right to left.)

In an acute scalene triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ and $N$ the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ of its circumcircle. Further, let $l$ be the circle with diameter $BC$ and let $D$, $E$ be the intersections of $l$ with the bisector of angle $BAC$. Points $F$, $G$ lie on the circle $l$ so that the quadrilateral $DEFG$ is a rectangle. Prove that the points $F$, $G$, $M$, $N$ lie on a circle.

In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ we have $|AB|=|BC|=|CD|$. Let $P$ be the intersection of its diagonals and let $O$, $Q$ be the circumcentres of triangles $APB$ and $DPC$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $OBCQ$ is a parallelogram.
Find all integers $n$ for which the number $$2^n+n^2$$ is the square of some integer.

In an attempt to colonise Mars, humanity has flooded the solar system with $50$ satellites, which have created $225$ communication lines among themselves (each line exists between one pair of satellites and no two satellites have more than one line between them). We say that a triple of satellites is connected if at least one of them has communication lines established with both of the other satellites. Determine the smallest and the largest possible number of connected triples of satellites.

Alica and Bohuš play a game on a board with $72$ cells arranged around the circumference of a circle. At the beginning, Bohuš places one token on each of some of the cells. In each round, Alica first chooses an empty cell and Bohuš must then move a token onto it from one of the adjacent cells. If he cannot do so, the game ends; otherwise the next round follows. Determine the smallest number of tokens for which Bohuš can ensure that the game lasts at least $2023$ rounds.

Let $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 3$ and let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be the side lengths of an arbitrary $n$-gon. Prove the inequality $$a_1+a_2+\dots+a_n>\sqrt{2\left(a_1^2+a_2^2+\dots+a_n^2\right)}.$$

In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $H$ be its orthocenter and $I$ its incentre. Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to the line $BC$ and let $E$ be the image of point $A$ under the point reflection with centre $I$. Further, let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ to the line $ED$. Prove that the points $B$, $H$, $F$ and $C$ lie on a circle.

Let $(a_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that for $n\ge 0$, $$a_{n+2}=a_0a_1+a_1a_2+\dots+a_na_{n+1}-1.$$
a) Prove that some prime divides infinitely many terms of this sequence.
b) Prove that there are infinitely many such primes.

In a triangle $ABC$, let $M$, $N$, $P$ be the midpoints of the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, and $G$ its centroid. Let the circumcircle of triangle $BGP$ meet the line $MP$ at a point $K$ different from $P$, and let the circumcircle of triangle $CGN$ meet the line $MN$ at a point $L$ different from $N$. Prove that $\angle BAK=\angle CAL$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n\ge 3$. Consider an $n\times n$ square grid whose individual unit squares can be either white or black. In each step, we change the colours of five squares forming the shape shown below, in any rotation. At the beginning all squares are white. Decide for which $n$ it is possible, after a finite number of steps, to make all the squares black.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/czsk_2023_p6_fig.png

Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive integers such that one of the values $$\gcd(a,b)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(b,c),\qquad \gcd(b,c)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(c,a),\qquad \gcd(c,a)\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$$ is equal to the product of the remaining two. Prove that one of the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ is a multiple of another one of them.
($\gcd(x,y)$ and $\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)$ denote the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple, respectively, of positive integers $x$, $y$.)

Let an interior point $P$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ be such that $$\angle PAD=\angle ADP=\angle CBP=\angle PCB=\angle CPD.$$ Let $O$ be the circumcentre of triangle $CPD$. Prove that $|OA|=|OB|$.

Determine the largest positive integer $n$ such that any set of $n$ tetrominoes, each of which has one of the four shapes in the figure, can be placed without overlapping into a $20\times 20$ table so that each tetromino covers exactly four cells of the table. The individual tetrominoes may be rotated and reflected arbitrarily.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/czsk_2024_p3_fig.png

$10$ boys and $10$ girls met at a party. Each boy likes a different positive number of girls. Each girl likes a different positive number of boys. Determine the largest non-negative integer $n$ such that it is always possible to form at least $n$ disjoint pairs in which each of the two likes the other.

Let $(a_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of real numbers such that for every non-negative integer $k$, $$a_{k+1}=3a_k-\lfloor 2a_k\rfloor-\lfloor a_k\rfloor.$$ Determine all positive integers $n$ such that if $a_0=1/n$, then this sequence is constant from some term on.
(By $\lfloor x\rfloor$ we mean the greatest integer not exceeding the number $x$.)

Find all right triangles with integer side lengths into which one can inscribe two congruent circles with a prime radius such that the circles are externally tangent to each other, both are tangent to the hypotenuse, and each of them is tangent to a different leg.

Real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ satisfy $$a+b+c+d=0$$ and $$\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c+\frac1d=0.$$ How many of the equalities $$\begin{aligned} ab&=cd,\\ ac&=bd,\\ ad&=bc\end{aligned}$$ can hold simultaneously?

Find the largest integer $n$ with the following property: Whenever five pairwise distinct points are given in the plane such that two of them lie in the interior of the triangle formed by the remaining three points, it is possible to label some three of these five points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ so that $n^\circ<\angle XYZ\le 180^\circ$.

Let $p$ be the largest prime dividing a positive integer $n$, where $n>1$. For every non-empty subset of the divisors of $n$ we write down the sum of its elements. Suppose that in this way we have written down more than $p$ numbers from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, p+2\}$ and that no number from this set has been written down more than once. Prove that no number has been written down more than once.

At least $3$ pairwise distinct primes are written around a circle. For every two adjacent primes we determine the largest prime dividing their sum. In this way we obtain, up to order, the same primes as those that were written. Find all possible initial sets of primes.
(For example, the primes $2, 7, 3, 11, 17$ in this order do not work, since the corresponding sums $9, 10, 14, 28, 19$ have largest prime divisors $3, 5, 7, 7, 19$, respectively.)

Find all positive integers $n$ with the following property: In an $n\times n$ square table it is possible to colour $2n$ cells so that no two of them share a side or a vertex and every row and every column contains exactly $2$ coloured cells.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $H$ be its orthocenter, $\omega$ its circumcircle and $O$ the centre of $\omega$. Further, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ and $D$ the intersection of the line $AH$ with the circle $\omega$ different from $A$. The line $DM$ meets the circle $\omega$ at a point $E$ different from $D$. Let $F$ be the intersection of the line $AE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $OME$ different from $E$. Prove that $|FH|=|FA|$.

Positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ satisfy $x^2+y^2+z^2=75$, and two of the three sums $x+y$, $y+z$, $z+x$ are at least $10$. Determine the smallest and the largest possible value of the remaining sum.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and let $T$ be its centroid. Let $P$ be a point of the shorter arc with endpoints $B$ and $C$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular from point $P$ to the segment $BC$. Let $X$ be the intersection of the line $QT$ with the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$, and let $S$ be the midpoint of the segment $PX$. Prove that $\angle BAP=\angle SAC$.

We say that a group of people is tri-acquainted if each of its members knows exactly three other members and the group cannot be split into two non-empty parts so that every member has all of their acquaintances in their own part. (Acquaintance is mutual.) Determine the largest positive integer $k$ such that $k\ge 3$ and there exists a positive integer $n$ such that from every tri-acquainted group with at least $n$ people one can choose at least $k$ people and seat them around a round table so that every two neighbours know each other.

Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct positive integers such that the numbers $a^2+1$ and $ab+1$ have the same sets of prime divisors. Prove that the number $a^2+b^2+2$ is divisible by the square of some prime.

Let $\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2026}\}=\{1, 2, \dots, 2026\}$ and let $a_{i+2026}=a_i$ for every positive integer $i$. Determine the smallest possible and the largest possible number of indices $i$ from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, 2026\}$ such that each of the $2026$ numbers $$\begin{gathered} a_i,\\ a_i-a_{i+1},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+a_{i+2},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+a_{i+2}-a_{i+3},\\ \vdots\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+\dots-a_{i+2023}+a_{i+2024},\\ a_i-a_{i+1}+\dots-a_{i+2023}+a_{i+2024}-a_{i+2025}\end{gathered}$$ is non-negative.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a hexagon inscribed in a circle with centre $O$ such that each two of its opposite sides are parallel. The lines $AB$, $CD$, $EF$ determine a triangle $\Delta_1$ and the lines $BC$, $DE$, $FA$ determine a triangle $\Delta_2$. Prove that the circumcentres of the triangles $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ are symmetric with respect to the point $O$.
